title: Session KV handle leak causing GPU OOMs and host fragmentation — triage, hotpatch, and customer remediation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Multiple customers (hosted + Dedicated pools + Private VPC deployments) reported sudden GPU OOMs and long-tail host memory fragmentation after rolling runtime-1.21. We identified a session-layer KV 'handle' lifecycle bug: handles referencing KV cache shards were not released on some reconfiguration/connection-failure paths, delaying GPU memory free and triggering allocator fragmentation over long uptimes. This ticket coordinates triage, a safety hotpatch, customer remediation steps, and a follow-up permanent fix with regression tests and observability improvements.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long-running dedicated pool (>= 48h) with mixed short/long sequence workloads. 2) Trigger intermittent client disconnects (network jitter) and concurrent model switch (policy-based routing). 3) Simulate heavy KV prefix churn (many distinct session keys). 4) Observe resident GPU memory not decreasing after inference batches complete; eventually host OOMs or GPU eviction. 5) Verify open handle counts via runtime /metrics endpoint (kv.session_handles_open > expected).
mitigation_actions: - Immediate hotpatch: add defensive decrement on session handle cleanup path and a guard to force-release handles after N reconnects (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4281). - Rolling restart of affected Dedicated pools and guided restart for Private customers. - For Hosted: apply hotpatch to canary region, monitor, then deploy cluster-wide. - Temporary quota increase and autoscaling enabled for impacted customers where restarts are delayed.

next_steps: Merge hotpatch and complete cluster-wide rollout for hosted within 24 hours
Schedule coordinated restart windows and apply patch for Dedicated customers with priority ordering
Ship an automated check in runtime healthwatch that alerts when kv.session_handles_open exceeds baseline for >15m
Design allocator compaction pass for runtime-1.23 to mitigate fragmentation without restart
Add regression tests for session disconnect + model switch paths and include in preflight suite
Prepare customer communication template and RC notes for affected tenants
notes: Trade-offs: hotpatch forces immediate handle release aggressively which may drop cached prefixes and slightly increase token cost in short term; acceptable to stop OOMs. Permanent fix will be conservative with correctness proofs and extended stress testing. Canary metrics to watch: kv.session_handles_open, gpu_memory_resident_bytes, runtime.alloc_fragmentation_ratio, p99 latency. For Private customers, provide a scripted restart and patch bundle; discuss offline upgrade windows to avoid data-plane disruptions.
